treatments.description: Electromagnetic conductivity (EC) survey data processing infrastructure — including clustering algorithms, GIS software licenses, and variable-rate prescription generation systems — to delineate 3-5 management zones per field based on soil texture, organic matter, CEC, and productivity gradients. This precision infrastructure replaces uniform whole-field management with site-specific nutrient prescriptions targeting the spatial variability that drives depletion in low-CEC zones.

treatments.monitoring: Collect tissue samples at key growth stages (V6 and R1 for corn; V3 and R3 for soybean) to verify nutrient uptake within sufficiency ranges. Compare soil test results pre-application and post-harvest; target soil test P and K values within ±10% of target levels. Track input cost per bushel produced by treatment zone; target ≥10% improvement in nutrient use efficiency within the first crop year. Review and adjust rates annually based on yield response data.
treatments.escalation: If tissue test values remain below the sufficiency range at R1 growth stage despite prescribed application, or if soil test trends show no improvement after 12 months of adjusted rates, escalate to a certified crop adviser (CCA) or soil scientist for diagnostic evaluation including root zone assessment and possible micronutrient panel. If yield response in treated zones is <3% above control after two crop cycles, review zone delineation and rate methodology.

treatments.label: Erosion Vulnerability Mapping from Soil Survey Training
treatments.description: Training on using the USDA Web Soil Survey to extract erosion hazard ratings, K-factor (soil erodibility), slope data, and T-factor (tolerable soil loss) for every field. Covers how to translate NRCS soil survey data into practical erosion management: identifying high-K-factor map units requiring immediate structural conservation, recognizing steep-slope inclusions within otherwise gentle terrain, and prioritizing fields where current management exceeds tolerable erosion rates.

treatments.label: EM38 Electromagnetic Induction Survey Equipment
treatments.description: Geonics EM38 or equivalent electromagnetic induction instrument mounted on a GPS-equipped ground vehicle for rapid, non-invasive mapping of apparent soil electrical conductivity across entire fields. EC values correlate with clay content, moisture, and topsoil depth — identifying erosion-thinned areas (low EC from exposed subsoil) and nutrient-depleted zones requiring targeted remediation through a single spatially continuous data layer.

treatments.label: Veris EC Sensor
treatments.description: Veris Technologies on-the-go soil EC sensor that measures shallow (0-12 inch) and deep (0-36 inch) apparent electrical conductivity simultaneously while being pulled across fields at 8-10 mph. Dual-depth measurement differentiates topsoil texture variation from subsoil conditions, enabling separate management zone maps for surface nutrient management and deeper erosion damage assessment where subsoil has been exposed by topsoil loss.

treatments.monitoring: Collect soil samples at 0-6-inch and 6-12-inch depths before implementation and annually thereafter; target measurable improvement in the primary metric (organic matter, aggregate stability, or nutrient level) within 3 years. Measure infiltration rate with a double-ring infiltrometer or timed ponding test at 3 representative points per field; target ≥15% improvement within 2 years. Document soil condition observations (compaction, earthworm counts, residue decomposition) at spring and fall tillage windows.
treatments.escalation: If the target soil health metric (organic matter, aggregate stability, or infiltration rate) shows no measurable improvement after 3 annual sampling cycles, escalate to a certified crop adviser (CCA) or soil scientist for comprehensive soil health diagnostic including biological assay, compaction profiling, and drainage assessment. If infiltration rate declines by >20% from baseline at any measurement point, investigate compaction or structural damage before the next field operation.

treatments.label: GIS Yield-Soil Overlay Analysis Tools
treatments.description: GIS software configured with multi-year yield map overlays, soil EC survey layers, and soil test interpolation surfaces for identifying zones where declining yields correlate with nutrient depletion patterns. Spatial correlation tools enable operators to distinguish yield loss from nutrient depletion (expanding low-CEC zones treatable with amendments) versus erosion damage (exposed subsoil requiring structural conservation), providing diagnostic evidence for targeted intervention planning.

issues.label: Soil Compaction
issues.summary: Heavy equipment traffic and wet-field operations creating hardpan layers that restrict root penetration, water infiltration, and biological activity

circuits.detail: Excessive tillage passes compacting soil structure below the plow layer
Microbial communities suppressed in anaerobic compacted zones, reducing nutrient cycling
Drainage capacity restricted by compacted subsoil layers blocking water movement
Cover crop root systems unable to penetrate hardpan for deep soil remediation
Soil chemistry distorted by poor aeration and waterlogging in compacted profiles

issues.label: Nutrient Depletion
issues.summary: Chronic extraction of soil nutrients without adequate replacement causing declining fertility, pH imbalance, and reduced crop response to inputs

circuits.detail: Cation exchange capacity declining as organic matter decreases and base saturation drops
Soil test values diverging from expected ranges despite standard fertilizer applications
Lime and gypsum amendments insufficient to correct accelerating pH drift
Compost and organic inputs unavailable in quantities needed to restore depleted soil carbon
Soil maps showing expanding zones of low productivity requiring site-specific remediation

issues.label: Erosion Crisis
issues.summary: Accelerated topsoil loss from wind and water erosion exceeding natural regeneration rates, permanently degrading field productivity

circuits.detail: Wind and water erosion removing topsoil faster than soil formation can replace it
Aggressive tillage exposing bare soil to erosive forces during vulnerable periods
Cover crop adoption insufficient to provide continuous ground cover through erosion windows
Soil biology disrupted as erosion removes the biologically active topsoil horizon
Soil survey maps rapidly outdated as erosion reshapes field-level productivity zones

issues.label: Salinization
issues.summary: Rising salt concentrations in the root zone from high water tables, poor drainage, or irrigation with saline water sources

circuits.detail: Soluble salt accumulation reaching phytotoxic levels that inhibit root water uptake
Drainage systems unable to flush salts below the root zone, causing progressive buildup
Gypsum and amendment applications unable to keep pace with salinization rates
Soil microbial diversity collapsing under osmotic stress from elevated salt concentrations
Standard soil tests failing to capture spatial variability of salt-affected zones

issues.label: Organic Matter Collapse
issues.summary: Rapid decline in soil organic carbon from intensive cropping without adequate residue return, threatening water-holding capacity and biological function

circuits.detail: Microbial biomass crashing as substrate availability drops below maintenance thresholds
Composting and organic amendment programs scaled back due to supply and cost constraints
Cover crop biomass insufficient to offset carbon losses from residue removal and mineralization
CEC declining as humus fraction disappears, reducing nutrient retention capacity
Erosion accelerating on degraded soils with poor aggregate stability from low organic matter
